themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints in East Flatbush surged to 3 THIS WEEK, a 380% increase versus the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a potential acute outbreak or food handling violation cluster that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (380% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Spike is fresh and concentrated in current reporting period, not a sustained trend
High statistical significance (z-score 4.91) indicates non-random event, not noise
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants or food vendors are generating complaints; cross-reference with DOH inspection records
Interview affected residents about symptoms and onset timing to determine if complaints cluster around specific establishment(s)
Investigate whether vendor enforcement spike (500% up) and food poisoning spike are linked—are unlicensed or non-compliant vendors operating?

themes_detail.label: Tree Overgrowth Emergency THIS WEEK
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints in East Flatbush reached 14 THIS WEEK, a 239% spike versus the 4.1 weekly average, with concurrent spike in tree-cutting requests (up 700%), suggesting a district-wide vegetation management crisis affecting sidewalk safety and pedestrian access.
evidence: 14 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly baseline (239% spike, z-score: 4.87)
3 new tree requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42) suggests complementary infrastructure failure
Sidewalk condition complaints also up 182% over 2 weeks (12 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.2 baseline), indicating interconnected street maintenance collapse
reporting_angles: Walk affected neighborhoods to document blocked sidewalks and branches encroaching on streets; photo-document safety hazards
Interview residents about maintenance requests pending; ask how long they've been waiting for city response
Investigate Parks Department capacity: are budget cuts or staff shortages preventing routine tree trimming, creating backlog?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints in East Flatbush jumped to 3 THIS WEEK, a 500% increase versus the 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks, suggesting a surge in unlicensed or non-compliant street vending that may overlap with the week's food poisoning spike.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Temporal alignment with food poisoning spike (same week) suggests possible causal link: unlicensed food vendors may be driving food safety complaints
High z-score (5.0) indicates statistically significant deviation, not background noise
reporting_angles: Map vendor enforcement complaints against food poisoning complaints to see geographic/vendor overlap
Interview NYPD and DOE enforcement officers about capacity and recent enforcement actions
Scout neighborhoods for unlicensed vendors; document non-compliance issues (lack of permits, improper food storage, poor hygiene)

themes_detail.label: House of Worship Noise Complaint Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints related to houses of worship in East Flatbush spiked to 5 LAST WEEK, a staggering 1233% increase versus the 0.4 weekly average, suggesting a sudden escalation in a single congregation's amplified events or a new venue opening without sound mitigation.
evidence: 5 house of worship noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% spike, z-score: 9.55—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Spike concentrated in single week; no indication of sustained multi-week trend, suggesting acute triggering event
Extreme z-score (9.55) indicates complaint concentration is highly non-random
reporting_angles: Identify which congregation(s) generated the 5 complaints; determine if they're running amplified events (services, celebrations, outdoor gatherings)
Interview complaining residents about timing, frequency, and duration of noise; establish noise level (decibel data if available from DOE)
Contact House of Worship leadership to understand if events have changed (new sound system, expanded capacity, extended hours)

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Maintenance Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints in East Flatbush rose to 12 over the PAST 2 WEEKS, a 182% increase versus the 4.2 weekly baseline, signaling deteriorating pedestrian infrastructure that parallels the tree overgrowth emergency and may indicate broader street maintenance collapse.
evidence: 12 sidewalk condition complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.2 weekly baseline (182% spike, z-score: 4.96)
Converges with overgrown tree/branch crisis (both week 2) and street condition complaints (417 total over 90 days), suggesting systemic maintenance failure
Z-score of 4.96 indicates statistically robust spike
reporting_angles: Conduct block-by-block audit of sidewalk conditions (cracked pavement, uneven surfaces, missing sections) in complaint hotspot areas
Cross-reference sidewalk complaints with DOT maintenance schedules to determine if district has deferred or delayed repairs
Interview residents and elderly/disabled pedestrians about trip/fall hazards and whether complaints have been ignored
